brief_summary: Hero art for the guides-pillar wireless keyboard buying guide (Bluetooth vs 2.4GHz dongle vs wired, latency focus). bearings.md's guide default (annotated keycap row) was adapted per an explicit brief instruction to a topic-specific motif: a top-down keyboard silhouette with a floating 2.4GHz USB dongle radiating a dashed signal fan toward the keyboard, plus a subdued wired USB-C cable in the lower margin as the neutral point of comparison — mirrors the split-ergo precedent of reinterpreting the keycap-row default when the topic calls for a more literal subject.

template: directive: simple line drawing + single splash of color illustrative of subject; guide subjects default to an annotated motif — reinterpreted here per explicit brief instruction as a keyboard + USB dongle + radiating signal-wave motif rather than a keycap row
subject: Top-down keyboard silhouette (12-column x 4-row key grid, bottom row with two modifier keys flanking a spacebar) in neutral warm-grey stroke, x=110-760. A small USB dongle (body + connector tab + transmit LED) floats free at upper right, dusty-rose stroke/fill, with three dashed concentric arcs fanning out from its connector tip toward the keyboard — the 2.4GHz wireless link, labeled '2.4GHz' in JetBrains Mono. Lower-left margin carries a subdued (opacity ~0.4-0.5), un-splashed USB-C cable + plug glyph labeled 'wired' in neutral warm-grey, the neutral point of comparison against the dongle's wireless link. No Bluetooth glyph included — the dongle specifically denotes the 2.4GHz-vs-BLE latency distinction that is the article's core claim.
alt: A top-down keyboard outline with a small USB dongle floating at its upper right corner, radiating a dashed fan of signal arcs toward the keyboard, labeled 2.4GHz. A subdued wired USB-C cable and plug sit in the lower-left margin, labeled wired, as the point of comparison.
